mentl/2298016:
Three defects, each found by the fix for the one before it.

1. The mechanism picked its readers' policy. driver_entry_with_ranges
   hardcoded diag_scope(ScopeModule(entry)), so every caller got a user
   verb's narrowing — including `mentl verify`, the medium's own board,
   the one reader for which narrowing IS the defect. Scope is a parameter
   now (driver_entry_scoped); the old entry delegates with the same
   value, so the ten-plus call sites are untouched.

2. The only unsuppressed compile had no modules. verify.sh grepped
   m2.err, and wheel.mn is every module concatenated into ONE file — 255
   import lines in a single module, where a cross-module reference
   problem is unconstructible. The leg reads the manifest link through
   the verb now. It reported 7, where the blob said 0 and the per-module
   sweep said 58; the gap is not slack, since a module checked alone
   links only what it imports.

3. Scope lookup was span containment across every module. Four of the
   seven were references to a function's OWN PARAMETERS, unresolved in
   that function's own comment. crc_fn_scopes builds a decl's extent as
   "my span to the next decl's" — true while spans were offsets into one
   weave, a cross-file claim once every module restarts at line 1: the
   last decl of module A ran to the FIRST LINE of module B. Scopes carry
   their module and stop at its edge; crc_scope_at matches module first,
   containment second. Hβ.cursor.module-of-a-span-is-containment meeting
   the prose gate — the same correction the caret took. 7 -> 3.

The last three were this landing's own comment listing the unresolved
names as examples; from that scope they are other functions' binders, so
they are written as prose — the sanctioned fix, not the dodge.

is the proof) and authored ref 739 -> 740 (the delegating wrapper's

mentl/2288cb7:
Every armed diagnostic deletes a category of guessing permanently, so the
arming path is the path out of the loop. E_EffectMismatch is the last crown
class unarmed. The licence is measured: the wheel's census of every error
class is 0, so the corpus channel is the only gate, and it carried 15
reports.

Two were honestly-wrong signatures and are fixed. mn-ev2 and mn-ev4 both
declared `fn outer(x) with G + D` while calling a mid declared
`G + D + Memory` — the author widened the callee and not the caller.
Exactly the mn-cli-dispatch shape that unblocked E_PurityViolated. 15 -> 13,
and both files left the battery's carrier list. Battery errors 19 -> 17.

The other 13 are not fixable by widening, and that is the finding.
mn-payload declares `with Probe` while the medium infers
`Memory + Alloc + Probe({alpha: Int, beta: Int, gamma: Int})` — a
type-parameterized instance. A with-clause takes value arguments; it cannot
say Probe({record}) at all, so no signature matches what inference proved.
The payload family carries most of the 13 for that one reason.

The blocker is Hβ.syntax.type-instance-in-with-clause — the same gap that
made mentl tighten author un-re-parseable rows at pin 1aca4868. The guard
there refuses to write what cannot be read back; this is that sentence from
the other side, the medium unable to declare what it can prove.

A second class measured unarmable, its follow-up named nowhere until now.
mn-resume-in-called-fn runs correctly at exit 9 while reporting
E_ResumeOutsideArm twice, and its own comment calls the fix "the named
follow-up" — which a grep of RESIDUE did not find, so by PLAN §7's law it
did not exist. The report is honest about the typing (resume : R -> S needs
the arm's continuation types, and inf_arm_tys answers None for a standalone
drive) and wrong about the program. Arming would refuse a correct fixture.
Banked as Hβ.infer.resume-in-a-called-fn-has-no-arm-types.

mentl/2233a63:
The decisive instrument ended the loop: the git-extracted historical
boot re-executed twelve times, 12/12 deterministic silence — the
original deferral finding was real, the corrective a true soundness
fix, and the refutation the measurement error (the mtime fallacy plus
an unstamped post-fix capture). The mechanism is attributed: a
non-member's deferred gate parked in a branch instance's infer_ctx
and died with the branch bracket. The process law lands whole: probe
results carry their boot sha, and cross-time comparisons re-run the
git-extracted binary, never trust mtimes.
mentl/22a4bbc:
Closes the H1.4 named follow-up at src/lower.nx:790 ("Single-handler-
per-op naming for now"). Multi-handler-per-op is wheel-canonical —
lib/prelude.nx has 10+ handlers all defining `yield`-arms for the
Iterate effect (map/filter/take/drop/collector/fold/for_each/any/all/
partition + inline handlers in fn bodies). Pre-substrate every arm
emitted `(func $op_yield ...)` at module level → wat2wasm rejects
with duplicate-fn-name; the wheel-scale "84,691 funcref entries
producing 4.9 GiB WAT" diagnosed in §4.5.10 was 10+ handlers each
independently emitting same-named arm fns, NOT DAG-shared LowFn
pointers (cfn_walk's wrong hypothesis).

Substrate change — lower handler arms with a discriminator threaded
from each caller:
  fn_name = "op_" ++ discriminator ++ "_" ++ arm.op_name

Discriminator sources:
  - HandlerDeclStmt(name, _, _) → name (top-level handler)
  - HandleExpr (inline anonymous) → int_to_str(handle) — graph-
    mint-unique by construction

Wheel-canonical (src/lower.nx):
  fn lower_handler_arms_as_decls(arms, discriminator) = ...
  HandlerDeclStmt(name, _, arms) → lower_handler_arms_as_decls(arms, name)
  HandleExpr(body, arms) → lower_handler_arms_as_decls(arms, int_to_str(handle))

Seed mirror (bootstrap/src/lower/{walk_handle,walk_stmt}.wat):
  $lower_handler_arms_as_decls (param $arms i32) (param $discriminator i32)
  fn_name = $str_concat($str_concat($str_concat(504, discriminator), 4400), op_name)
  Underscore separator string at data offset 4400 (free per audit;
  past 4360+20=4380 highest existing data segment).

Empirical (sanity):
  effect E { op() }
  handler h { op() => 42 }
  → (func $op_h_op ...) — was (func $op_op ...)
  Module-level symbols unique by construction.

wat2wasm error surfaces the next residue: $main's `(call $op_op)`
from LPerform doesn't match (the symbol is `$op_h_op` now). Named
peer Hβ.first-light.lperform-handler-discriminator carries the
matching update at perform sites — monomorphic LPerform threads
handler_name from row

sonido/2247f74:
make plugins installed sonido_delay.clap while bundle-clap.sh, releases,
and the docs all name the artifact sonido-delay.clap. The dash names are
now the single convention, which the VST3 story depends on: a wrapper

two-top/222c856:
The findings-ledger audit turned up something worse than the width
note: no checksum components were ever registered, so the desync
detection configured in Phase 12 has been exchanging trivially equal
checksums every 30 frames since it shipped — the detector could not
fire. The interval was real; the comparison was vacuous.

The width-portable hasher moves from replay_sync's private guts into
net (one implementation, byte-identical — the committed golden test
is the proof), and the app registers the fingerprint set replay_sync
already columns: positions, velocities, dash, stun, boomerangs, score,
match state, and the rolled-back RNG, all hashed width-stably so a
future browser peer compares like with like against a phone.
Registration lives in the app crate, not SimPlugin — it is online
bookkeeping, and the sim stays untouched. Observing a live mismatch
fire remains a loopback/operator step; the web pages' vanishing
failure notices ride along fixed (a tape-drop error now outlives the
boot screen instead of dying with it), and join.html tells a
warm-open phone to dial by hand — the running app cannot see new
intents, and pretending otherwise would be a silent no-op.
